title: Seabright Capital - Private VPC Discovery
next_steps: Ethan to send security & SOC2 docs and network diagram link
Priya to share pilot runbook and staging test plan
Customer to provide VPC CIDR and list of required egress IPs by 2026-11-20
action_items: Ethan (Redwood AE): Email pricing and contract template (due 2026-11-20)
Priya (Redwood SE): Share detailed network diagram and AWS PrivateLink vs VPC peering comparison (due 2026-11-19)
Mark (Seabright): Export VPC CIDRs, account IDs, and desired regions (due 2026-11-20)
summary: Intro discovery covering Seabright's requirements for a private VPC deployment. Main concerns: network connectivity (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), egress/static IPs, region constraints (eu-west-1), KMS integration, and SOC2/audit controls. Agreed next steps include exchanging diagrams, security docs, and scheduling a pilot kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate your time. quick intros?
[00:08] Mark (Seabright): Mark here, head of infra, we run core platform and networking. Laura's our CISO, Samir handles platform engineering, Jenna does the application side.
[00:18] Ethan: Great, I'm Ethan, AE for Redwood Inference, with Priya and Carlos from our SE team. goal for today is to understand your network and security constraints for a private VPC deployment.
[00:28] Priya (SE): Hi all. we'll cover connectivity options, required ports, egress behavior, and how we integrate with your KMS. feel free to interrupt.
[00:36] Jenna: sounds good. quick note - we're targeting eu-west-1 for data residency, that's non-negotiable.
[00:42] Priya: noted. eu-west-1 only, ok. can you outline your desired topology? peering, transit gateway, or private endpoints?
[00:50] Mark: Our preference is to avoid public internet egress. we currently peer to some SaaS via transit gateway and we have strict egress controls. ideally we want either cross-account VPC peering or PrivateLink endpoints.
[01:04] Carlos: Got it. two common patterns. VPC peering gives direct route-level connectivity but is cross-account routing and has some limitations with transitive routing. PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) exposes a private endpoint in your VPC and keeps traffic on the AWS network, usually simpler for restrictive networks.
[01:22] Samir: what's the tradeoff on latency and cost? we are very sensitive — trading a few ms matters for-sync inference in some workflows.
[01:30] Priya: in our experience latency difference is often small; peering can be slightly lower latency because it's route-based, but PrivateLink adds a small proxy hop and can be marginally higher. cost wise PrivateLink has per-hour + per-GB charges, peering is just data transfer. depends on throughput.
[01:48] Laura (CISO): we also need to ensure that keys never leave our control. KMS integration is critical — can Redwood work with our customer-managed KMS for model encryption and logs?
[01:58] Priya: yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS integration. we'll need to coordinate IAM roles and trust policies for the control plane to access wrapped keys; we often recommend envelope encryption where your keys wrap Redwood-managed keys or vice versa depending on the model. we'll share the KMS runbook.
[02:16] Mark: ok, also curious about egress IPs — we use allowlists for external services like S3 replication. will Redwood provide fixed egress IPs?
[02:24] Carlos: for Private we can provide static egress IPs from our NAT/egress pool in your VPC or via a managed NAT in our side depending on the topology. typical pattern: with PrivateLink, traffic exits through the endpoint owner; with peering, traffic remains in your VPC, so egress IP is yours. we should map this to your firewall rules.
[02:44] Jenna: so with peering we'd keep full control over outbound nat right?
[02:48] Priya: correct. peering means your routing controls egress. PrivateLink typically terminates at an endpoint service we host, so you'd need to allow their egress IP/ranges; we can provide those for allowlisting.
[02:59] Mark: any constraints about cross-region? our data for EU must stay in eu-west-1. can Redwood guarantee region isolation and not fallback to hosted nodes in us-east-1?
[03:10] Ethan: yes, we support region pinning for private deployments. we can scope the deployment strictly to eu-west-1. the fallback policies can be disabled for compliance. we'll document the SLA and region controls.
[03:22] Laura: audit/logging — we need detailed audit trails and retention for at least 7 years for some records. does Redwood provide audit logs and are they integrable with our SIEM?
[03:32] Priya: we ship audit logs and event streams. for Private we can push logs to your S3 bucket or to an endpoint in your VPC via a connector; integrating with your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) is common. retention policies we can configure or you can pull to your long-term store.
[03:47] Mark: how about network ports — what ports does the runtime need open?
[03:50] Carlos: primarily HTTPS 443 for control/management. for model binary pulls we may use S3 endpoints (443). gRPC or internal traffic between instances uses ephemeral ports inside the VPC and is handled by our orchestrator. we'll provide a minimal list.
[04:06] Jenna: any special requirements for KV cache or persistent storage? we're worried about latency and cross-AZ hops.
[04:12] Priya: KV cache is local to the serving cluster in the region and uses high-throughput local interconnects; for Private it will be in your VPC/AZs so cross-AZ latency is your cloud's standard. we recommend collocating call origins and serving AZs for best latency.
[04:26] Samir: can we run a small pilot on our staging VPC? we'd like to run 10 qps of inference and measure p95 latency with our prompts.
[04:34] Ethan: absolutely — pilot is the best next step. Priya will provide a staging runbook and test plan.
[04:40] Priya: for pilot we'll need a cross-account role or peering setup, VPC CIDR ranges, and a list of subnets to host endpoints. we can provide Terraform snippets for the peering/endpoint setup.
[04:53] Laura: security review process — we'll need SOC2 bridge, pen test reports, and data flow diagrams.
[04:58] Ethan: we'll send SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. we can also coordinate a security questionnaire (we've done SIG, CAIQ).
[05:07] Mark: curious about upgrade/rollout behavior. when Redwood patches the runtime, will that trigger restarts that affect our SLA?
[05:14] Carlos: we support canary rollouts and A/B routing; for Private you control maintenance windows. we can do nondisruptive upgrades depending on capacity. documented in the ops runbook.
[05:25] Jenna: what about model artifacts? we want private model weights in our S3 and not copied to other places.
[05:30] Priya: yes, we can pull from your S3 and run inference without copying outside your VPC. for some managed models we may use read-only pulls into the compute layer; we'll discuss the exact model onboarding flow.
[05:44] Samir: do you support peered accounts across multiple AWS orgs? we have a multi-account setup via AWS orgs.
[05:50] Priya: yes, cross-account peering and PrivateLink across accounts is supported; we'll need account IDs and permissions. transit gateway setups also work for complex topologies.
[06:00] Laura: encryption in transit, at rest, and in use — any homomorphic or confidential compute options?
[06:07] Carlos: in-use confidentiality is limited; we do support customer-managed KMS for at-rest and TLS 1.2+ for in-transit. for strict 'in-use' confidentiality there's limited off-the-shelf solutions; we can discuss hardware-backed HSMs or bring-your-own HSM for key control but fully homomorphic compute isn't broadly production-ready.
[06:26] Ethan: ok wrapping up: agreed next steps — exchange CIDRs and account IDs, Redwood to send security docs and pilot plan, schedule pilot kickoff next week.
[06:36] Mark: great — send that to the list and we'll aim to have the infra details by Friday.
[06:40] Ethan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and action items.
[06:44] (end)
